title: Air conditioning debate highlights UK housing regulation concerns
summary:
Environmental restrictions on air conditioning in new residential developments have sparked debate about regulatory burdens on UK housing delivery. A North London estate agent has highlighted planning system challenges affecting housing supply and affordability.

title: Liverpool estate agency launches AI property valuation tool
summary:
A Liverpool-based estate agency has launched a free AI-powered property valuation service that aims to address what its founders describe as widespread overpricing in the UK housing market. The tool analyses live sold prices, local demand data, crime statistics, flood risk information, and energy performance ratings.

title: Leeds letting agent dismissed after benefits discrimination claims
summary:
A Leeds-based letting agency has terminated an employee following the emergence of a recording in which the staff member appears to discuss filtering out prospective tenants who claim benefits. The practice is now explicitly prohibited under the Renters' Rights Act.

title: Ground rent cap implementation brought forward to 2027
summary:
The government will introduce a £250 annual cap on residential ground rents in England and Wales by late 2027, a year earlier than previously planned. The accelerated timeline affects more than four million leaseholders following pressure from MPs and parliamentary committees.

The post Ground rent cap implementation brought forward to 2027 appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Family support accounts for £11bn in first-time buyer funding
summary:
More than half of first-time buyers in the UK require financial support from family members to purchase their first property, with total family contributions reaching £11 billion including inheritance. The data from Savills shows 53% rely on family assistance through gifts, loans, or inheritance, whilst 64% draw on their own savings.

title: UK mortgage affordability reaches tightest level since 2008
summary:
UK homebuyers are now spending 21.3% of gross household income on initial mortgage repayments, the highest proportion since 2008. Regional disparities show North Norfolk, Hillingdon and Luton face the most acute affordability pressures.

The post UK mortgage affordability reaches tightest level since 2008 appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: FCA proposes mortgage rule changes for wider borrower access
summary:
The Financial Conduct Authority has published proposals to reform mortgage lending rules, aiming to expand access for first-time buyers, self-employed workers and older borrowers. The consultation remains open until 28 July 2026.

The post FCA proposes mortgage rule changes for wider borrower access appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Scottish estate agent ordered to amend comparative adverts
summary:
The Advertising Standards Authority has ordered RE/MAX Property Specialists in Scotland to amend comparative advertising after ruling that claims made against named competitors breached advertising standards. The regulator found several claims were misleading and not adequately substantiated.

The post Scottish estate agent ordered to amend comparative adverts appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: First-time buyers face rising stamp duty burden
summary:
Thirty per cent of first-time buyers in England purchased homes exceeding £300,000 in 2026, double the proportion recorded a decade ago, according to analysis by Connells Group. The increase marks the highest level on record and represents a significant shift in the tax burden facing new homeowners.

title: Estate agents adopt AI platform for lead generation
summary:
Estate and lettings agents are deploying AI-powered platforms to capture property enquiries outside traditional office hours, as buyer search behaviour shifts from search engines to AI assistants. Jaiyn.ai has launched with pricing set at £50 per month plus VAT, targeting small and medium-sized agencies.
